description: Multi-agent AI assistant that classifies a natural-language calendar/email request and routes it to one specialist agent, each grounded by real tool calls and traced end-to-end in Langfuse. Built as an Applied Agentic AI capstone project.

tech_stack.fine_tuning: none -- behavior governed by per-agent system prompts (src/calendarmate/prompts/*.md) plus code-level guards for anything exactly computable

entry_points.name: pytest suite
entry_points.description: Deterministic keyword assertions per agent. Live tests (calling the real OpenAI API) are skipped automatically without OPENAI_API_KEY set.
entry_points.known_flaky_test: one live-model test occasionally fails due to run-to-run model variance, not a real bug

entry_points.name: Evaluation harness
entry_points.description: Runs the full case set through the real end-to-end pipeline (classification + dispatch + grounded generation) and grades each response with an LLM judge against that case's specific criteria. Distinct from pytest: pytest makes deterministic keyword assertions calling each agent directly; the harness judges natural-language output against prose criteria through the full pipeline.
entry_points.date_pinning: date.today() is patched to 2025-06-17 for briefing.py/email.py/scheduler.py so June-2025 fixture requests stay reproducible regardless of the real wall-clock date

entry_points.name: Live CLI
entry_points.description: Real Google Calendar and Gmail account, one request per invocation. Kept entirely separate from run_orchestrator's mocked default -- pytest and harness.py never touch this file or the real account.

orchestrator.name: Orchestrator

functions.route_request: classifies the request into exactly one label, never generates the final answer
functions.run_orchestrator: calls route_request, looks up the matching agent in _DISPATCH, calls it, returns its answer unmodified

orchestrator.fallback_behavior: an unclassifiable request (empty label, or one outside the 5 routes) raises ValueError inside route_request; run_orchestrator catches it and returns FALLBACK_MESSAGE instead of crashing -- found via the harness's T15 edge case, where the live classifier once returned an empty string and took down an entire run

agents.name: Briefing Agent
agents.grounding: the tool is the only source of event data the model is given -- conflict detection is exact-overlap math in Python (calendar_tool.find_conflicts), never model judgment
key_features: day-name disambiguation: a weekday matching today's own weekday is asked about explicitly rather than guessed
weekday labels are computed in Python and returned by the tool (never asked of the model) after a real request mislabeled a date's weekday

agents.name: Scheduler Agent
agents.grounding: availability/conflict checks are exact overlap math in plain Python; only create_event has a side effect

extended_capabilities.conflict_resolution: names the conflicting meeting and offers a concrete trade-off (different time, move/shorten the existing meeting, or go async) instead of a bare refusal

cancellation.ownership_check: code-enforced -- refuses to cancel a meeting whose owner != the requesting user, regardless of what the model decides
cancellation.lookup_grounding: cancel_event is refused for any event_id the model didn't just receive from a find_meeting_to_cancel call in this same request
cancellation.confirmation_rule: unconditional two-step confirmation (lookup, then a separate confirming reply) -- deliberately stricter than every other rule in the app; this specific rule is prompt-enforced only, a known accepted limitation, not code-enforced
cancellation.pending_confirmation_state: a small gitignored .pending_cancellation.json lets live_assistant.py bridge the required two-step confirmation across two separate, otherwise-stateless CLI invocations

recurring_meetings.mechanism: structured recurrence fields (frequency, weekdays, until) are compiled into a real RRULE string in Python (_build_rrule) -- the model never writes RRULE syntax itself
recurring_meetings.mandatory_end_date: an open-ended series can never be created -- 'how long should this repeat' is treated as missing information
recurring_meetings.known_limitation: only the first occurrence's availability is ever checked; a conflict on a later occurrence in the series is not automatically caught

extended_capabilities.auto_generated_title: the meeting title is the one field the Scheduler fills in itself (e.g. 'Meeting with Bob') rather than asking for, without ever inventing a topic/agenda
extended_capabilities.timezone_handling: a named timezone is treated as descriptive only; the hour/minute given is passed through unchanged and never converted, after a real booking once landed at the wrong wall-clock hour
extended_capabilities.past_time_refusal: a same-day time at or before the current time (an injected now parameter) is refused outright, never booked
extended_capabilities.off_hours_refusal: code-level guard (_is_off_hours) refuses an unconfirmed weekend/before-8am/after-6pm booking -- moved into Python after three prompt-only attempts each caused an unrelated regression
extended_capabilities.same_time_as_existing_meeting: can resolve 'same time as my standup' by reusing find_meeting_to_cancel as a read-only lookup, while still asking for attendees and surfacing the requester's own guaranteed self-conflict

agents.name: Email Agent
agents.model_rationale: the only agent on the full model, not gpt-4o-mini -- its action-required/FYI classification judgment call needed a stronger model after two prompt-only tuning rounds fell short (one of which backfired by hallucinating content)
agents.grounding: get_emails is the sole source of which emails exist, preventing invented senders/subjects

extended_capabilities.needs_attention_pool: every unread email regardless of age, plus every email read within the last 5 days (negotiated with the user before implementing) -- widens the candidate pool without weakening the unread-mail guarantee
extended_capabilities.reply_detection: a read email that the user has already replied to (checked via the Gmail thread's last message) is excluded from needs-attention, since a reply already sent is a stronger signal than recency
extended_capabilities.self_sent_exclusion: an email whose sender is the user's own authenticated address is filtered out before classification, so the user is never flagged as waiting on their own reply
extended_capabilities.large_pool_batching: classifies at most 15 emails per call via a forced-tool-call schema and merges results in Python, after a single freeform call on a 49-email pool was found to silently drop one item
extended_capabilities.date_range_vs_unread: get_emails takes optional start_date/end_date to answer 'what came in last week' distinctly from 'what's unread' -- a needs-attention request never mistakes a period word like 'today' for a receive-date filter

agents.name: Follow-Up Agent
agents.grounding: get_meeting_record is the only source of a meeting's attendees/notes, preventing invented action items

extended_capabilities.real_notes_source: for the real integration, notes are read from an attached 'Notes by Gemini' Google Doc first, falling back to the Calendar event's description field
extended_capabilities.html_email_formatting: the drafted Markdown body is converted to real HTML before sending, so bold/bullets render correctly in Gmail instead of showing literal ** characters
extended_capabilities.sender_exclusion: the sender is filtered out of the email's own recipient list in code, and the send is refused outright if that would leave zero recipients
extended_capabilities.draft_and_send_together: an explicit send request is drafted and sent in the same reply rather than pausing to ask 'shall I send this'

agents.name: Digest Agent
agents.description: Has no tools or LLM call of its own -- concatenates Briefing's and Email's independently grounded answers under '### Calendar' / '### Email' headings. Deliberately not a third synthesizing LLM call, since two already-correct answers stitched together carries no hallucination risk where an extra pass would.

real.isolation: an independent, parallel implementation of the same tool shapes -- no environment flag or runtime branch could accidentally make a test touch a real account

observability.setup_reference: built using the official Langfuse skill (github.com/langfuse/skills), installed under .claude/skills/langfuse/
observability.untraced_entry_point: pytest -- tests/conftest.py explicitly sets LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENABLED=false, since real credentials are otherwise available to that process too

instrumentation.root_span: one per real request (run-orchestrator for harness, handle-request for live_assistant)
instrumentation.per_generation_naming: every client.create() call carries a name= matching its enclosing span, gated by a sys.modules check so it's safe whether the real Langfuse-wrapped client or a plain test client is passed in

user_id_scheme.harness: fixed 'capstone-test-user' for every case, since this is a mocked eval run, not a real account
user_id_scheme.live_assistant: the real authenticated Google account email, resolved once per invocation

observability.cost_note: the Email Agent's gpt-4o (vs every other agent's gpt-4o-mini) plus its batched classification calls (up to 15 emails per batch, multiple batches per large inbox) is the primary cost driver visible in the dashboard -- confirmed intentional, not a leftover default

testing.pytest_last_known_result: 162/162 (occasionally 161/162 due to one documented flaky live-model test)
testing.live_tests_gate: OPENAI_API_KEY must be set in .env, else live tests are skipped automatically
testing.date_injection: agent-level tests pin `today=`/`now=` explicitly so results never depend on the real wall-clock date

known_limitations: Cancellation's confirm-before-acting rule is enforced by the prompt only, not by code -- a deliberate, disclosed exception to this project's usual code-level enforcement of safety-critical checks, since it depends on a genuinely separate prior turn a stateless function has no way to verify on its own
A recurring series' availability check only covers its first occurrence, not every future date the series would land on

No sensitive-data masking is applied to Langfuse traces -- a conscious choice for a personal, single-user project where the same calendar/email content already reaches OpenAI on every request regardless of tracing
real_world_verification_highlights: Booked, then found and deleted, real events that landed on the wrong day/hour before the date-lookup-table and timezone-passthrough fixes
Created a real recurring series (weekdays, through a fixed end date) and confirmed occurrence dates and the shared recurringEventId via the Calendar API
Looked up and correctly refused to cancel a real meeting owned by someone else
Sent a real follow-up email and read back the raw HTML body to confirm formatting and recipient exclusion
Confirmed real 'needs attention' fixes against the live inbox: self-sent mail excluded, already-replied mail excluded, payment reminders surfaced with exact real amounts/dates
note: This project is hand-coded Python rather than built in a visual workflow tool (n8n/Make/Flowise), so nothing here was literally exported -- this file is a hand-authored, structured description of the same system covered in CLAUDE.md and the architecture diagram, provided to satisfy machine-readable workflow documentation requirements.
